subproblem.title: Stationarity in integral form is equivalent to vanishing first variation of mass (Simon 2.4)
subproblem.statement: Assume (GF) (for every n ≥ 1, ℓ and every rectifiable n-varifold V: μ_V is finite on compacts, dim T_xV = n μ_V-a.e., and x ↦ p_{T_xV} is μ_V-a.e. strongly measurable) and FirstVariationFormula. Then StationaryIffVariational holds: for n ≥ 1, every pair a and every open U, V = mk a is stationary in U (∫ div_M X dμ_V = 0 for all C¹ fields X with compact support in U) if and only if t ↦ (imageMass a (φ t) K).toReal has derivative 0 at t = 0 for every compact variation (φ, ε, K) with K ⊆ U.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ), 0 < n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts V.weight ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, Module.finrank ℝ (V.tangentSpace x) = n) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection) V.weight) → FirstVariationFormula → StationaryIffVariational
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions (used throughout). n ≥ 1 and ℓ ≥ 0 are integers, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, Hⁿ = μHE[n] (equal to Simon's Hⁿ), B_ρ(ξ) = closedBall ξ ρ (closed ball), ω_n = omega n ∈ (0, ∞), and Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ for every n-dimensional subspace P. For a rectifiable n-varifold V: μ = μ_V = V.weight; T_x = V.tangentSpace x; p_x and p_x^⊥ are the orthogonal projections onto T_x and T_x^⊥; div_M X(x) = V.tangentialDiv X x = trace(DX(x)∘p_x); ∇^M h(x) = V.tangentialGradient h x = p_x(∇h(x)); r = |x − ξ|; q_ξ(x) = V.normalRadialSq ξ x = |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|² ∈ [0, 1] (q_ξ(ξ) = 0 because division by 0 is 0); w_ξ(x) = q_ξ(x)/|x − ξ|ⁿ (w_ξ(ξ) = 0); a_ξ(ρ) = μ(B_ρ(ξ))/ρⁿ (a real number); Θ(ξ) = V.density ξ. A test field in U is a C¹ map X: E → E with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U (IsTestField). 'V has mean curvature H in U' (HasMeanCurvatureIn) means H ∈ L¹_loc(U, μ) and ∫div_M X dμ = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every test field X in U; 'stationary in U' means ∫div_M X dμ = 0 for every test field X in U. (FV) for V means: (FV1) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K; (FV2) dim T_x = n for μ-a.e. x; (FV3) x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. (GF) is the statement that (FV) holds for every n ≥ 1, every ℓ and every V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ (exactly the second conjunct of the sibling tangent_structure_first_variation); (AT) is the contract Prop ApproxTangentAE. Under (FV): q_ξ, w_ξ, ∇^M h (for h ∈ C¹(U), on U) and div_M X (for X ∈ C¹) are μ-a.e. strongly measurable, being continuous functions of p_x and of continuous data; |div_M X| ≤ (n+ℓ)‖DX‖ and div_M X = 0 off tsupport X, so div_M X is μ-integrable for every test field X; μ is a locally finite, hence outer regular, Borel measure, and μ(E ∖ spt μ) = 0 (spt V = spt μ).

Source: Simon Ch. 4, 2.4: 'of course by 2.2 this is equivalent to the requirement ∫ div_M X dV = 0 for any C¹ vector field X on U having compact support in U.' The printed one-line argument is made precise: a C^∞ compactly supported field is realized as the initial velocity of the variation φ_t(x) = x + tX(x), and C¹ fields are reached by mollification, using (GF) to pass to the limit in the integrals.

Hypotheses: (GF) and FirstVariationFormula (FVF). Fix n ≥ 1, ℓ, a pair a = (M, θ), V = mk a, μ = μ_V, and an open set U. For a variation φ write X_φ(y) := deriv (t ↦ φ t y) 0.

1. (⇒) Assume V is stationary in U and let (φ, ε, K) satisfy IsCompactVariation φ ε K with K ⊆ U. Since φ is C^∞ on the open set (−ε, ε) × E, X_φ is C^∞, in particular C¹. For y ∉ K, φ t y = y for all t ∈ (−ε, ε), so X_φ(y) = 0; hence the support of X_φ lies in K, tsupport X_φ ⊆ K (K is compact, hence closed) ⊆ U, and X_φ has compact support. Thus X_φ is a test field in U and stationarity gives ∫ div_M X_φ dμ = 0. By FVF, t ↦ (imageMass a (φ t) K).toReal has derivative ∫ div_M X_φ dμ = 0 at t = 0.

2. (⇐), C^∞ fields. Assume the right-hand side and let X: E → E be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U. Put L := sup_y ‖DX(y)‖ < ∞, ε := 1/(L + 1), φ(t, y) := y + tX(y) and K := tsupport X (compact). We check IsCompactVariation φ ε K: ε > 0; K is compact; (t, y) ↦ y + tX(y) is C^∞; for |t| < ε the map φ_t is injective because |φ_t(y) − φ_t(y')| ≥ (1 − |t|L)|y − y'|, and surjective because for z ∈ E the map y ↦ z − tX(y) is a contraction with constant |t|L < 1 whose fixed point y satisfies φ_t(y) = z; Dφ_t(y) = I + tDX(y) is invertible since ‖tDX(y)‖ < 1, so by the inverse function theorem the inverse of the bijection φ_t is C^∞, and Function.invFun φ_t is this inverse; φ(0, y) = y; for y ∉ K, X(y) = 0 and φ(t, y) = y. Moreover K ⊆ U and X_φ = X. By FVF, m(t) := (imageMass a (φ t) K).toReal has derivative ∫ div_M X dμ at 0, and by hypothesis it has derivative 0 at 0; derivatives are unique, so ∫ div_M X dμ = 0.

3. (⇐), C¹ fields. Let X be a test field in U: C¹, compact support, K_0 := tsupport X ⊆ U. Since K_0 is compact and U is open there is δ > 0 with K_1 := {y : dist(y, K_0) ≤ δ} ⊆ U (any δ > 0 if U = E); K_1 is compact. Let η_k ≥ 0 be C^∞ mollifiers with ∫ η_k = 1 and spt η_k ⊆ B_{1/k}(0), and X_k := η_k * X (componentwise convolution). For k > 1/δ: X_k is C^∞, its support lies in K_0 + B_{1/k}(0) ⊆ K_1, so tsupport X_k ⊆ K_1 ⊆ U is compact; and DX_k = η_k * DX → DX uniformly on E, because DX is uniformly continuous with compact support. By step 2, ∫ div_M X_k dμ = 0 for k > 1/δ. For every linear A and orthogonal projection p, |trace(A∘p)| ≤ (n + ℓ)‖A‖, so |div_M X_k(y) − div_M X(y)| ≤ (n + ℓ) sup_E ‖DX_k − DX‖ for all y, and both functions vanish off K_1. By (GF), div_M X_k and div_M X are μ-a.e. strongly measurable (continuous functions of DX_k(y), DX(y) and p_y), bounded, and supported in K_1 with μ(K_1) < ∞, hence μ-integrable, and |∫ div_M X dμ| = |∫ (div_M X − div_M X_k) dμ| ≤ (n + ℓ) sup_E ‖DX_k − DX‖ μ(K_1) → 0. Therefore ∫ div_M X dμ = 0 for every test field X in U, i.e. V is stationary in U. Steps 1–3 prove StationaryIffVariational.
proof_key_steps: (⇒) The initial velocity of a compact variation with K ⊆ U is a C^∞ test field in U; FVF gives derivative ∫ div_M X dμ = 0
(⇐) For C^∞ compactly supported X, φ_t(x) = x + tX(x) is a compact variation for |t| < 1/(sup‖DX‖+1) (contraction + inverse function theorem); uniqueness of derivatives gives ∫ div_M X dμ = 0
(⇐) For C¹ test fields, mollify: X_k → X in C¹ uniformly with supports in a fixed compact K_1 ⊆ U; (GF) gives integrability and |∫ div_M X| ≤ (n+ℓ) sup‖DX_k − DX‖ μ(K_1) → 0

audit.reason: GF and FirstVariationFormula are explicit antecedents. Initial velocities prove the forward implication; the compact variations x+tX realize smooth fields, and mollification with uniform derivative convergence proves the converse for C¹ fields. The proof does not assume this equivalence.
